chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about ghusl of janābah, and he said: “You begin by washing your hands, then pour with your right hand onto your left, then wash your private part and your forearms, then rinse your mouth and draw water into your nose, then wash your body from the top of your head to your feet. There is no wudu (ablution) before it nor after it. Everything to which you cause the water to reach, you have purified. And if a man were to immerse himself in water in a single immersion, that would suffice him, even if he did not rub his body.”

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it would suffice him; it would fulfill the requirement
key_terms.ارْتِمَاسَةً وَاحِدَةً: a single complete immersion in water
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath performed to remove the state of janābah
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ: your private part, to be washed during the procedure
key_terms.كَفَّيْكَ: your two hands, washed at the beginning of the ghusl
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: ritual ablution, stated here as not separately required before or after this ghusl

ai.seo_question: How should ghusl al-janābah be performed, and does it require separate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the method and legal sufficiency of ghusl al-janābah. It states the order of washing, clarifies that separate wudu (ablution) is not required before or after this ghusl, and affirms that a single full immersion in water is sufficient if the body is covered by water.
